cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If the caretaker asks why we had the cake cupboard open, we were checking the lock. You remember that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember you eating the cake while I held the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eating isn't what the key was for. Keep the explanation attached to the question, please: we checked the lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's going to ask why half the cake's gone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we checked the contents as well. Don't say 'half'; we didn't measure it. Try that again.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 prompts a shared maintenance recollection. A3 corrects B2's answer scope, and A5 treats B4's missing cake as an inspection while correcting the unmeasured quantity and asking repetition.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 remembers eating during access; A3 tries to exclude it by question scope. B4 predicts the actual cake question; A5 broadens the rehearsed version to include contents.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies an inconvenient true memory and B4 predicts an obvious consequence of visible missing cake. B's concern follows the event rather than inventing crumbs in a lock.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's missing-half question to widen the story and apply even more absurd measurement precision to the admitted consumption.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies cupboard access and caretaker; B2 identifies eating with B holding the door; B4 identifies missing cake as the likely evidence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's don't-say-half direction targets B4's exact wording and enables rehearsal; the humor comes from selective precision.

coach2.situation: A1 identifies cupboard access and caretaker; B2 identifies eating with B holding the door; B4 identifies missing cake as the likely evidence.
coach2.stated: A1 cupboard was opened; B2 held the door while A ate cake; B4 expects missing cake to be noticed.
coach2.inferred: A is minimizing incriminating recollections, not making a trustworthy maintenance report.
coach2.missing: No crumbs must be imagined inside hardware in this revision.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; new information is ordinary missing food rather than unexplained physical geometry.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 challenges A1's maintenance memory with the eating they witnessed.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 restricts the explanation to A1's opening question after B2 adds cake.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 predicts a different question that A3's narrow explanation cannot answer.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 revises the shared story and corrects B4's half measure before asking a repeat.

reservation: A3 uses a technical-sounding distinction that is not morally or logically exculpatory. The character's priorities, rather than the evaluator, justify it.
